text: Given valid required-only arguments (invited_user_email_address, invite_redirect_url), when graph_create_invitation is called, then POST /invitations is issued with invitedUserEmailAddress/inviteRedirectUrl/sendInvitationMessage=true and the tool returns invited_user_id, invite_redeem_url, and status sourced from Graph's response
notes: Model after users.py's graph_create_user / graph_create_tap pattern.

text: Given send_invitation_message=False, when the tool is called, then the request body carries sendInvitationMessage=false
Given send_invitation_message is omitted, when the tool is called, then the request body carries sendInvitationMessage=true (the default)
Given invited_user_display_name is supplied, when the tool is called, then the request body carries invitedUserDisplayName with that value

Given message_language, customized_message_body, and cc_recipients are all supplied, when the tool is called, then the request body carries invitedUserMessageInfo with messageLanguage, customizedMessageBody, and ccRecipients built from the email list, each shaped as {"emailAddress": {"address": ...}}
Given none of message_language/customized_message_body/cc_recipients are supplied, when the tool is called, then the request body has no invitedUserMessageInfo key at all (not an empty object)
The registered tool schema for graph_create_invitation requires exactly invited_user_email_address and invite_redirect_url

Given Graph returns 403 Insufficient privileges, when the tool is called, then the result is {"error":{"code":"unauthorized","retryable":false,...}} via the connector's existing GraphError/_classify mapping
Given Graph returns 400 Bad Request (malformed invitedUserEmailAddress), when the tool is called, then the result is {"error":{"code":"invalid_argument","retryable":false,...}}

Given a fake Graph response whose invitedUser.id is some GUID, when the tool is called, then the tool's invited_user_id output equals that same GUID string unchanged -- the exact shape graph_assign_groups's user_id parameter expects, with no added prefix/wrapping
notes: This is the ticket's actual end-to-end ask: invite then graph_assign_groups with no extra lookup, matching Rewst's invite_result -> add_group_member flow.

text: Given a fake Graph response representing an existing-guest scenario (e.g. status other than PendingAcceptance), when the tool is called, then it passes the response straight through its normal curated-field mapping with no special-case branching

Given a token lacking User.Invite.All, when the tool is called against a fake client returning 403, then the result is unauthorized -- this connector's only gate is the real backend POST /invitations call, there is no UI menu-gating layer to fool
notes: Permission/multi-tenant anchor (S6 quality line), kept distinct from TC8 so AC9 has its own traceable case.

text: After the change, the repo's own three-way consistency test passes with the new tool present and consistent across the live tools/list registry, docs/gdap-role-map.yaml, and the README Tools table, and the hard-coded role-map count assertion is bumped from 45 to 46
notes: Existing test; passes automatically once EXPECTED_TOOLS, the yaml entry, the README row, and server registration are all added consistently. Also bump tests/test_gdap_role_map.py:79's assert len(role_map) == 45 to 46.

text: End-to-end against a real Entra tenant: invite a real external email address, confirm a guest user (userType: Guest) is created, confirm the invitation email arrives when send_invitation_message=true, and the inviteRedeemUrl opens Microsoft's redemption page
steps: Obtain a real Graph access token with User.Invite.All for a test tenant
Call graph_create_invitation with a real external test email address and a real inviteRedirectUrl
Check the Entra admin center for a new guest user with userType=Guest and the expected email
If send_invitation_message=true, check the external mailbox for the invitation email
Open the returned invite_redeem_url and confirm it reaches Microsoft's redemption page
expect: A guest user is created in the tenant, the invitation email is received when requested, and the redemption URL is valid
notes: No real vendor/tenant test account is available to the design or dev leg. Per mcp-track.md S3, missing a vendor test account does not block shipping; record a Known Gaps README bullet instead, same convention as this connector's other real-tenant-pending tools (graph_start_cloud_sync, the calendar tools).
